name: Hampi and Badami
one_line: North Karnataka plains, from the ruins of Hampi to the rock-cut temples of Badami, Pattadakal and Aihole

highway.value: NH 50 (through Hosapete); NH 367 (through Badami); State Highway 14 (Badami to Pattadakal)

source.title: Hampi – Places to Visit, History & Travel Guide |…

fuel.note: Pumps are those drawn on the open map within the search radius of the road. A pump missing from the map is missing here, so each gap is a worst case.

rules.title: Hampi: no private vehicles near the Vittala temple
rules.detail: Motorcycles stop at a parking area about one kilometre short. Visitors walk or take an electric cart. No government order was found.
rules.set_by: Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority

rules.title: Hampi: ticket for the Vittala temple
rules.detail: The state tourism office gives about 40 rupees for Indian visitors and says most other temples are free. The temple opens 8:30 am to 5:30 pm.

source.title: Hampi – Places to Visit, History & Travel Guide |…

season.note: The state tourism office names October to March; from March to June the plains reach 40 degrees, and rain falls from July to October.

authorities.announces: Tickets and opening hours for protected monuments

hazards.title: Heat on the plains
hazards.detail: Summer days reach 40 degrees at Badami. Ride early and carry water.

hazards.title: Monkeys at Badami
hazards.detail: Large troops live around the caves and town. Keep food and loose items packed away.

gaps: No government order or official page found for the vehicle restriction at the Vittala temple; the source is a travel blog.
The ticket office website of the Archaeological Survey of India would not load its monument list, so ticket prices for Badami, Pattadakal and Aihole are not recorded.
No rule specific to motorcycles found anywhere on this route, and no two-wheeler parking fee from an official page.
No source found for stretches without fuel between Hosapete and Badami.
No source found for the usual number of days riders take.
No highest point recorded: this is a plains route. Badami stands at 1,920 feet.
No office found that announces road closures for this route.
Filming dates of the two videos are not known.
